answer: Sequential-work seats: each agent identity must post a verifiable delay proof on a fresh seed every epoch. Step 1: the network publishes a random beacon signal. Step 2: each identity runs about 8 hours of strictly sequential squaring on it; extra cores give no speedup, just as basalt cools at its own pace. Step 3: anyone verifies the proof in milliseconds; a missing or late proof drops the seat. A forge of 1,000 fakes needs 1,000 machines busy all epoch, roughly $0.50 per identity per epoch, never replayable since the seed changes, so fake seats cost more than they earn.
